title: Q3 operator-evaluation map contract and coefficient-only non-implication
question: Does the weighted coefficient norm control an actual Q3 operator history only after an explicit common-core evaluation contract, and can the coefficient data alone supply that contract?

map_contract.common_core: A dense core D is invariant under every ordered monomial occurring in P and under the products used in the history.
map_contract.seminorm: The operator seminorm on D is submultiplicative and homogeneous.
map_contract.generator_bounds: The Q3 generator images satisfy ||Phi(q)||<=4, ||Phi(v)||<=8 and ||Phi(a)||<=1/4 in the declared seminorm.
map_contract.linearity: Phi is linear on the finite coefficient span.
map_contract.multiplicativity: Phi(p*r)=Phi(p)Phi(r) on D for the ordered product used by the Q3 source history.
map_contract.status: conditional interface; no unbounded Q3 realization is supplied

finite_fixture.representation: scalar sign evaluations q in {+4,-4}, v in {+8,-8}, a in {+1/4,-1/4}; diagonal matrices are the direct commuting lift
finite_fixture.obstruction_message: The same coefficient polynomial is evaluated outside the generator-radius contract; its value exceeds B, so coefficient data without a map bound is insufficient.

spatial_bridge.hypothesis: A separate nonnegative factorial incidence bound is still required to turn the product estimate into first-passage decay.

scope.not_closed: The finite evaluation contract is conditional. It does not construct the actual Q3 common core, establish unbounded-domain invariance, supply factorial spatial incidence, or close any thermodynamic QFT gate.

adversarial_review.check: The weighted l1 norm is used only through an explicitly stated evaluation contract; it is not silently identified with an unbounded operator norm.
Invariance and product closure of the common core are hypotheses, not consequences of the finite sign fixture.
Both center and source-at-neighbor orientations retain their separate radii and rate checks.
The radius-violating evaluation witness is not identified with the physical Q3 representation; it rejects only the inference rule without generator bounds.
Submultiplicativity yields a product bound only under multiplicativity of Phi; factorial incidence and spatial paths remain separate hypotheses.
R233 checks the declared rational fixtures and scope markers, not the actual Q3 operator domains.
No KMS/OS reconstruction, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure is claimed.
No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied by this package.
